stem: Why are mid-dermal burns described as 'non-blanching'?

options.text: The superficial dermal capillary plexus has been damaged.
The burn has reached the subcutaneous fat layer.
The nerve endings have been completely destroyed.
There is a total lack of keratinocytes in the deeper layers.

explanation: Non-blanching occurs because the vessels responsible for the white-to-pink color change are no longer functional or have extravasated blood.
rationale: Consider the status of the blood vessels located in the transition zone between the epidermis and dermis.

optionExplanations.A: Non-blanching occurs because the vessels responsible for the white-to-pink color change are no longer functional or have extravasated blood.
optionExplanations.B: Reaching the fat layer would characterize a full thickness burn, not a mid-dermal burn.
optionExplanations.C: Nerve damage affects sensation, but the blanching characteristic specifically refers to the status of the blood supply.
optionExplanations.D: Mid-dermal burns still have some surviving epidermal remnants in hair follicles and glands, though the capillary plexus is compromised.

source.hint: Consider the status of the blood vessels located in the transition zone between the epidermis and dermis.
